card.name: Bugaku
card.tagline: Stately masked court dance performed to gagaku music
card.profile: Bugaku is the ceremonial court dance of Japan, performed to gagaku music for over twelve hundred years, marked by slow, precise and regal movements, elaborate embroidered costumes and masks, on a roughly 6-by-6-yard platform (Wikipedia, Bugaku). Britannica describes its two basic forms: 'dances of the left' (saho no mai), accompanied by togaku derived from Chinese music and danced in red costumes, and 'dances of the right' (uho no mai), accompanied by komagaku from Korea in blue/green costumes, often performed alternately as paired dances (tsugaimai) (Britannica).
card.insight: Britannica notes Bugaku's repertoire derives from dance forms imported from China, Korea, India and Southeast Asia - making it, with its allied music gagaku, among the oldest surviving court dance-and-music traditions in the world.
aliases: Saho no mai / Uho no mai
